newsitem.title: FRANCE: RALLYING-SAINZ AND DELECOUR IN CLOSE DUEL IN CORSICA.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-SAINZ AND DELECOUR IN CLOSE DUEL IN CORSICA.

text.p: Spaniard Carlos Sainz and Frenchman Francois Delecour were locked in joint first place in the Tour of Corsica rally after Tuesday's eventful second day that saw world champion Tommi Makinen's hopes ruined.

Sainz, in a massive, four-wheel drive Ford Escort, and Delecour, in a lightweight, two-wheel drive Peugeot 306, had exactly the same time after the day's six timed stages in changing conditions with occasional downpours.

Frenchman Gilles Panizzi, the overnight leader, was third, nine seconds back in the second Peugeot while Briton Colin McRae was fourth, a further 10 seconds behind and also still in contention for victory on Wednesday.
McRae lost time in the morning because of a wrong choice of tyres but then recovered superbly, clocking the best time in four tests in his Subaru Impreza.

Finn Makinen, who started the day in sixth position, had to pull out after bumping into a cow with his Mitsubishi Lancer halfway through the day's first test, the longest of this year's rally over 48.9 kms from Vero to Liamone.
Neither Makinen nor co-driver Seppo Harjanne was hurt but the car was destroyed and they were unable to restart.
Tuesday's gruelling first section on twisting asphalt roads north of Ajaccio went to Sainz, who gained 46 seconds on Panizzi.
Delecour clocked the second fastest time, 10 seconds slower than Sainz, while Panizzi slipped to third.
"I made the wrong choice of tyres," explained Panizzi, who kept up with the pace in the following timed stages to keep his chances alive.
Sainz, who was second, four seconds behind Delecour after Liamone, was slightly faster than the Frenchman in three of the next four stretches despite electrical problems.
"The windshield wipers stopped working at one point while it was pouring and the horn blew by itself for some reason but apart from that, everything was fine," said the Spaniard.
With one timed stage left in the day, Sainz was six seconds ahead of Delecour.
But in the last section to Carbuccia, the Frenchman, cheered on by noisy fans lining the roads, gained six seconds on his rival to set up an exciting finale.

Sainz and Delecour were not the only ones to shine as McRae was the fastest in the day's second test to Piana along the Mediterranean island's dramatic rocky coastline and again in the last three sections in the mountains overlooking the port of Ajaccio.
With the top four covered by fewer than 30 seconds, a hard-fought battle was expected on the last day of the rally.
"I have a good feeling with the car and it's not over yet," warned McRae.
"In such conditions, things can change very fast," said Sainz. "When it's sometimes wet and sometimes dry, tyre choice is essential. Anything can still happen."
